analysis: Docs-only PR: docs/reference/ssd-kv-cache.md changes the 'Last updated' date (line 3) and adds a table row at head line 119 describing provider-staged complete-checkpoint imports. Those imports now create destinations from zeroed host bytes and skip eval/stream fences, so staging no longer waits on MLX-Swift's process-wide evalLock. The row also says the import plan charges the largest destination as staging scratch. I found no changes to encryption, DBK3 format, HMAC lookup tags, TTL or disk budget, cache scope, or the SEC-035 acceptance, so T-041 mitigations are unchanged on this evidence. Availability and memory-accounting behavior (no lock contention, scratch charge for the zero-source commit outside the MLX allocator) is described only in docs. The implementing sources named in the row were not supplied: CheckpointHostZeros.swift, CompleteCheckpointTransfer.swift, PagedCheckpointStorage.swift and CompleteCheckpointImportPlan.swift. I cannot verify the claims. A source-level pass should confirm that the zero-fill creates no cross-tenant residual data, that the scratch charge is correct, and that the host-memory bound holds under the GlobalKVCacheBudget (relevant to T-028 and T-041). The patch excerpt was marked incomplete but the range map is complete. No finding is raised, since this is a documentation update that cannot itself regress security.
